findings.title: Recomputing activations is a large part of the step
findings.evidence: 3433 ms per step (16% of module time) is forward work done a second time by checkpointing
findings.lever: keep more blocks un-checkpointed (trainer.checkpoint_by=measured with tune_checkpointing, attention_fraction) if memory allows

findings.title: Much of the module time has no cost model
findings.evidence: 2775 of 8318 ms is in modules the cost model does not know

findings.title: The step is launch bound
findings.evidence: the device is busy 58% of the step (794 of 1371 ms) over 32938 launches and 214712 operators per step, 213 us of host time per launch
findings.lever: graph replay (trainer.graph=true) removes the launch cost if the capture can use the same kernels

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: linear ff.net (up)
findings.evidence: 206.3 ms per step against an ideal 5.6 ms (3% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 5374 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: linear attn2.to_v (up)
findings.evidence: 197.0 ms per step against an ideal 0.9 ms (0% efficient, memory-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 5374 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: linear attn2.to_k (up)
findings.evidence: 196.5 ms per step against an ideal 0.9 ms (0% efficient, memory-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 5374 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn1 (up)
findings.evidence: 194.0 ms per step against an ideal 6.0 ms (3% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 5374 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Slowest pieces by recoverable time: attention transformer_blocks.attn2 (up)
findings.evidence: 180.4 ms per step against an ideal 6.0 ms (3% efficient, compute-bound), 36 layers; all rated pieces together leave 5374 ms
findings.lever: see the module table for the individual layers

findings.title: Dtype and copy kernels take a large share
findings.evidence: 21% of device time is casts and copies
findings.lever: find the modules issuing `.to(dtype)` round trips (autocast boundaries, adapter branches) and keep one dtype through them

findings.title: Many small memory-bound kernels
findings.evidence: 40% of device time (20410 calls per step) is elementwise, normalisation, copy, memory and reduction work
findings.lever: fusion (fewer, larger kernels): norm + modulation, activation + multiply, cast + matmul input; half the time is the most a fusion usually recovers

findings.title: The int8 path's own kernels are a large share
findings.evidence: rotate, quantize and dequantize kernels are 19% of device time against 213 ms of matmuls
findings.lever: int8_grad=int8 (no weight dequantize in backward), or a fused rotate+quantize in the kernels project; native weights if memory allows

findings.title: Some steps in the window were much slower than the rest
findings.evidence: 1 step(s) took over twice the median: step 20 (2, 68, 92) 5661 ms
findings.lever: a latent shape seen for the first time costs kernel and primitive creation (seconds); fewer distinct shapes (buckets.max_shapes) and a longer warm-up

findings.title: Module times do not add up to the device time
findings.evidence: modules account for 8318 ms of 794 ms device time per eager step
findings.lever: the difference is work outside the hooked modules (loss, optimizer, data movement) or host waits; see the phase and category tables
